jobs.title: Consultant, Human Health Risk Assessment and Community Health
jobs.description:
Company Description

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Job Description

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.

Ramboll is seeking an entry-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

Your new role

As an entry-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

Qualifications

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your professional development and advancement in the company! Successful candidates will typically possess:

Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology
Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 + years of relevant experience may be considered.
Strong analytical, quantitative, organizational, problem-solving, critical thinking skills, and time management skills; excellent written and oral communication skills
2+ years of chemistry coursework required.
Current authorization to work in the United States on a full-time basis, where required for the position.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
GIS capability is a plus.
Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Meaningful, high-impact work
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Competitive compensation and benefits
Professional development and leadership opportunities
A collaborative and inclusive culture
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $79,040–$98,800 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

Ready to join us?

If you are passionate about scientific excellence, environmental health, and community impacts, we would love to hear from you.

Please submit your application. Be sure to include all relevant documents including your resume, transcripts, a writing sample and cover letter.

jobs.title: Regulatory Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
Our client, manufacturing and mining operations
is seeking a Regulatory Environmental Specialist to join their team. As a Regulatory Environmental Specialist , you will be part of the Safety, Health & Environmental (EHS)
function supporting site operations
. The ideal candidate will have strong program management
, clear communication and training delivery
, and detail-oriented compliance execution
which will align successfully in the organization.

Job Title:
Regulatory Environmental Specialist

Location:
, Corona, CA (100% onsite)

Pay Range: $25 to $32 p/h on w-2

Duration: 12 month contract

Shift:
8-hour core hours between 7am-3pm PST, with some flexibility needed +/- 1-2 hours to be available for other shifts.

What's the Job?

Conduct defined technical and/or project tasks within the safety/environmental field to support successful completion of assigned projects.
Advise operations on EHS risks and controls, helping teams implement new or improved safety and environmental programs.
Engage in safety projects by partnering with operations to define project parameters, desired results, and action status updates to stakeholders.
Present and provide EHS training, including respirator fit testing and communication of IH results.
Facilitate and manage MSHA and other agency inspections and inquiries, including coordination of required sampling (IH, water, etc.).

What's Needed?

BS or MS graduate with an accredited degree in engineering sciences or a related field.
Applicable EHS program management experience of 3–5 years minimum.
Experience in the mining industry, including experience with Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA).
Self-directed, detail oriented approach with strong interpersonal, communication, coaching, prioritization, and organizational skills.
Analytical and strategic planning skills, including program development and deployment and the ability to lead cross-functional teams.

What's in it for me?

Own meaningful EHS work that directly supports safer operations through inspections, audits, and program improvements.
Build credibility with operations by translating EHS risks into practical controls and actionable guidance.
Strengthen your compliance expertise by coordinating MSHA and agency inspections and inquiries.
Develop your training and communication impact through respirator fit testing and EHS training delivery.
Work in a structured schedule with clear core hours and defined site shift coverage.

Upon Completion Of Waiting Period Consultants Are Eligible For

Medical and Prescription Drug Plans
Dental Plan
Vision Plan
Health Savings Account
Health Flexible Spending Account
Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account
Supplemental Life Insurance
Short Term and Long Term Disability Insurance
Business Travel Insurance
401(k), Plus Match
Weekly Pay

If this is a role that interests you and you'd like to learn more, click apply now and a recruiter will be in touch with you to discuss this great opportunity. We look forward to speaking with you!

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Health Officer
jobs.description:
About the role

An exciting opportunity exists for an enthusiastic and experienced environmental management professional to lead our motivated and collaborative team of Environmental Officer’s at Bathurst Regional Council. The Senior Environmental Officer will have a minimum of 5 years’ experience in a similar role and be capable of implementing policies, procedures and programs that both educate the community and assist Council to protect and enhance the local environment.
It is essential that the successful candidate is an excellent communicator as they will provide technical and policy advice to internal and external stakeholders and be confident in negotiating conflict to achieve satisfactory outcomes.
Key Requirements

Bachelor Degree in Environmental Health or Science
A minimum of five year’s experience in the monitoring and inspection of premises to ensure compliance with Public Health and Environmental Standards
Demonstrated ability to prepare warning letters, notices, orders and Penalty Infringement Notices under various Acts
Demonstrated capacity to provide specialist technical advice in the assessment of development applications relevant to Environmental Health
Solid working knowledge of the Food Act 2003, Public Health Act 2010, Local Government Act 1993 and associated regulations
Ability and experience in the mentoring and supervision of staff
Advance written and verbal communication and customer service skills
Advanced negotiation and conflict resolution skills
Organised and committed to continuously improving systems, procedures and policies
Demonstrated experience in providing timely and technically sound advice to staff, businesses and the community in environmental health matters
Intermediate user of MS Office applications, Mitti (iAuditor), Intramaps and industry specific programs
Demonstrated proficiency in the use of various IT hardware for both office and field based applications
Willingness to work outside of ordinary business hours to complete inspections when required

What We Can Offer

Work/Life Balance
enjoy a rostered day off every third week to recharge and reset
Generous Leave Entitlements
to support your personal and family needs
Fitness Passport
to stay active and healthy
Training & Development
to expand your skills
Employee Assistance Program
for confidential support services
Relocation Support

To view the Position Description click here

This position requires a pre employment health assessment which includes a functional, audio and drug & alcohol screen

Salary:
$1,809.00 to $1,900.57 per week (dependent on skills, qualifications and experience) plus superannuation and a leaseback vehicle
Position Status:
Permanent - Full Time 
Hours of work:
35 hours per week with an RDO every third week
Application closing date:
Sunday, 1 November 2026, at 11.59pm
Contact Officer:
Anna Stapleton, Manager Environment - 6333 6268
How to Apply?

To apply, please click Apply. There are screening questions that must be answered to apply for the position. You will need to upload a Resume to complete the application.

You can save and return to your job application at any time prior to the closing date. Unfortunately, applications that are not completed by the closing date and time will not be considered.

Your application information will be kept confidential in line with the Privacy Amendment (Private Sector) Act 2000 and the Privacy and Personal Information Protection Act 1998.

Bathurst Regional Council is committed to being a flexible, safe, equal and inclusive workplace where diversity is embraced and supported.

As an Equal Opportunity employer, we encourage applications from people who are from different backgrounds including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, people of any age, race, ethnicity, religion, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation and cultural background. 

Bathurst Regional Council is committed to being a Child Safe organisation with a zero tolerance for child abuse.
